group_assessment.primary_group_note: The Aqeilan laboratory again, this time with a clinical pathology arm — 83 osteosarcoma specimens from 51 patients, scored by immunohistochemistry. That mix is unusual for this corpus, where the group's work read so far is cell and mouse biology, and it is what makes the paper's own negative result (below) worth more than its positive one.
group_assessment.weighting: OBSERVATIONS in the clinical arm carry real weight: 83 specimens, 12 normal controls, exact binomial confidence intervals, Fisher's exact test against normal bone. The cell-line and mouse arms are ordinary. INTERPRETATION needs one specific discount, and it is not about rigour: the paper's own paired human analysis fails to show the association its Figure 5 title asserts, the authors say so in the Results, and the failure is reported only in a supplementary table. Where the text and the figure title disagree, the text is the one that was written last and hedged.

corpus_crossquery.query: Does a figure title in this corpus ever generalise beyond what the paper's own text says the data support?
corpus_crossquery.finding: 🔴 YES, AND THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE AND THE FIRST WHERE THE PAPER ITSELF PRINTS THE REFUTATION. Figure 5 is titled 'Inverse association of WWOX and RUNX2 expression in osteosarcoma' — a claim about the disease. The Results text, two paragraphs later, states: 'Although WWOX and RUNX2 results suggested an inverse association in human OSs, this was not evident when paired comparisons were performed on the 56 available cases'. And the numbers that follow run the OTHER WAY: 78% (7/9) of WWOX-strong pre-treatment biopsies were also RUNX2 POSITIVE, and 55% (6/11) of WWOX-reduced biopsies were RUNX2 NEGATIVE — both are same-direction co-occurrence, not inverse. The figure whose title generalises to 'in osteosarcoma' contains only cell lines and two illustrative stained sections. This differs from PMID 27308504 and PMID 31075076, where the compression was of MODALITY: here the modality is intact — the authors hedge properly in the text — and what travels beyond the evidence is the SCOPE of the title. DL-METH-094 should gain scope alongside modality, and this instance is the reason.

The HOS stable-clone rescue: colony formation, soft agar, migration and Matrigel invasion. It is the strongest functional claim in the paper and the one a therapeutic reading would lean on hardest. The most expensive of the three waivers.

figure_coverage.supplementary_gap: 🔴 THE SUPPLEMENT IS NOT RETRIEVED AND IT CARRIES THE PAPER'S OWN REFUTATION. One 5.8 MB PDF holding Supplemental Figures 1-6 and Supplemental Tables 1-9. Also there: Supplemental Fig 1, the micro-CT method behind '100% of Wwox-deficient mice had developed OS by 18 days-of-age'. A supplement that holds the refutation of a main-figure title is not an appendix, and this reading is partial because of it.

entries.proposition: THE CLINICAL HEADLINE, and it is the strongest thing in the paper: WWOX is absent or reduced in more than half of osteosarcoma specimens, against 12 normal bone and cartilage controls, with a p value from Fisher's exact test. Quoted from the Discussion rather than the abstract because the abstract is separated from the body by the validator and a quote taken there could not be verified against this surface.
entries.snippet: We find that WWOX expression is absent or reduced in 58% of OS patient specimens

entries.proposition: THE DIRECTIONAL CLINICAL OBSERVATION THAT MATTERS MOST FOR A TUMOUR-SUPPRESSOR READING, because it is longitudinal within patients rather than cross-sectional: WWOX comes BACK after chemotherapy and is LOST again in metastases. Two opposite movements of the same marker in the same patients is a far stronger argument than a single prevalence figure.
entries.snippet: In some OS patients, chemotherapy restored WWOX levels and the metastases had reduced levels

entries.proposition: PANEL SIDE, CONFIRMING — the metastasis arm of the sentence above, read from the pixels. What the panel shows is qualitative and the text does not overstate it; recorded because it is the one place in this paper where the clinical claim is visible rather than tabulated, and because a reader should know the comparison is between two different sections stained separately, which is an intrinsic limit of immunohistochemistry and not a defect of this figure.

entries.proposition: CONTRADICTION SET, MEMBER 2 OF 3 — THE CAPTION, which states the same comparison as the panel's own summary. Authored prose in the declared text surface, verified character-for-character. Note what it does NOT name: of the ten lanes in the blot it accounts for five.
entries.snippet: HOS, Saos2 and KHOS (WWOX-reduced) cells have higher levels of RUNX2 compared to MC3T3 and K7M2 (Wwox-positive) cells
entries.anchor: Figure 5 caption, item A. Declared surface body: authored prose in the declared artifact, not a pixel observation.

entries.proposition: 🔴 CONTRADICTION SET, MEMBER 3 OF 3 — THE PANEL, READ FROM THE PIXELS, AND IT DOES NOT SHOW WHAT THE SENTENCE AND CAPTION CLAIM. The claim requires MC3T3 and K7M2 to carry reduced RUNX2. In the blot both carry CLEAR RUNX2 BANDS, comparable to HOS, which the same caption places on the RUNX2-high side. The only lane with genuinely absent RUNX2 is MCF7 — a breast line, not an osteosarcoma line. AND THE PANEL HOLDS A LANE THE PAPER NEVER MENTIONS: ROS appears between MG-63 and U2OS, carries the strongest RUNX2 signal in the entire blot, and is named neither in the caption nor anywhere in the Results paragraph, which accounts for nine of the ten lanes. cited_panel_check holds: Figure 5A is the panel both the sentence and the caption cite. This is a contradiction of the stated comparison, not of the paper's thesis — the WWOX-low human lines HOS, SAOS-2 and KHOS do carry high RUNX2, and MCF7 versus MDA-MB231 does run inverse. What fails is the specific contrast the caption builds the claim on.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 5, panel A, read from files/fulltext/PMID20530675_Kurek2010_assets/f5.jpg at its native 1050x779, upper region. TEN lanes, labelled left to right: MCF7, MC3T3, K7M2, HOS, SAOS-2, MG-63, ROS, U2OS, KHOS, MDA-MB231. Three rows labelled at the left: RUNX2, WWOX, GAPDH. In the RUNX2 row the MCF7 lane is blank; MC3T3 and K7M2 both carry distinct bands of intensity comparable to HOS; ROS carries the darkest band in the row; SAOS-2, U2OS and KHOS carry strong bands; MDA-MB231 carries a band. In the WWOX row MCF7 is strongest, KHOS is faint and MDA-MB231 is faintest. GAPDH is even across all ten lanes.
entries.anchor: Figure 5, panel A, all ten lanes and three rows, read at 1050x779
entries.contradicts_needle: MC3T3 and K7M2 express Wwox and have reduced Runx2
entries.cited_panel_check: SATISFIED, verified on the pixels. Figure 5A is the panel cited by the body sentence at entries[3] and described by the caption at entries[4]. The falsifying observation is in the panel they both name.

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE PAPER PRINTS ITS OWN REFUTATION OF THE FIGURE'S TITLE, IN THE RESULTS, WHERE THE FIGURE IS TITLED 'INVERSE ASSOCIATION … IN OSTEOSARCOMA'. The paired human comparison does not show the association. This is what separates this instance from the modality compressions recorded in PMID 27308504 and PMID 31075076: there the hedge was removed, here the hedge is INTACT and what travels beyond the evidence is the SCOPE of a title — a claim about osteosarcoma, on a figure containing cell lines.
entries.snippet: Although WWOX and RUNX2 results suggested an inverse association in human OSs, this was not evident when paired comparisons were performed on the 56 available cases
entries.anchor: Results, 'Aberrant RUNX2 expression in human osteosarcoma'. The reference to Supplemental Table 8 follows.

entries.proposition: THE NUMBERS RUN THE OTHER WAY, AND THEY ARE IN THE RUNNING TEXT. If the association were inverse, WWOX-strong tumours should be RUNX2-negative. Seven of nine were RUNX2 POSITIVE. Recorded because a negative stated in words is easy to read past, and a negative stated as 78% is not.
entries.snippet: In pre-treatment biopsies, 78% (7/9) of WWOX strong tumors were also RUNX2 positive
entries.anchor: Results, 'Aberrant RUNX2 expression in human osteosarcoma', immediately after the sentence at entries[6]

entries.proposition: THE BOUNDARY THE AUTHORS DRAW INSIDE THEIR OWN CELL-LINE ARM, quoted because it is the honest half of the same paragraph the contradiction sits in: two of the osteosarcoma lines do not follow the correlation, and the authors say so. A reader who takes only the figure title would not know that either.
entries.snippet: the inverse correlation between WWOX and RUNX2 was not observed in two less differentiated OS cell lines, MG-63 and U2OS
entries.anchor: Results, 'Loss of WWOX expression is associated with elevated RUNX2 levels in several OS cell lines'

entries.proposition: THE MOUSE PREMISE, AND WHERE ITS EVIDENCE LIVES. The claim that every Wwox-deficient mouse develops osteosarcoma by 18 days rests on a micro-CT screening method described in a supplementary figure that is not retrieved. Recorded at the evidential level it actually has: a strong number whose method this reading has not seen.
